question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with normal vector $\overset{~}{n},$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨y,\,x-z,\,-2x⟩\,,\,\overset{~}{n}(x,y,z)=⟨2x,\,-z,\,y⟩\,,\,n=\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}\frac{\boxed{}}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}S
$$

what is the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

To compute the above dot product, we must normalize the vector $\overset{~}{n}.$ By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖} \\  & =\frac{⟨2x,\,-z,\,y⟩}{\sqrt{(2x)^{2}+(-z)^{2}+(y)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨2x,\,-z,\,y⟩}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+{z}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨2x,\,-z,\,y⟩}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨y,\,x-z,\,-2x⟩\cdot \frac{⟨2x,\,-z,\,y⟩}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{⟨y,\,x-z,\,-2x⟩\cdot ⟨2x,\,-z,\,y⟩}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2xy-z(x-z)-2xy}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{{z}^{2}-xz}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\,\frac{{z}^{2}-xz}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}S.\end{aligned}
$$
